31.22.5.en: St. Ambrose She maketh for herself embroidered coverings.

31.23.0.en: Her clothing is silk and purple [22].

31.23.1.en: The virtuous woman makes embroidered coverings, that is, carpets which she lays on the floor for the comfort of her household and guests, or special coverings for the family.

31.23.2.en: She wears white linen garments (silk) and costly purple; the first points to her cleanness and purity through receiving the righteousness of Christ, and the second also points to the royal nature which she enjoys.

31.24.s.en: F. Because of her, her husband is honored among the elders

31.24.0.en: Her husband is known in the gates, when he sitteth among the elders of the land [23].

31.24.1.en: He who chooses a virtuous wife receives honor for his prudence and balance, as well as for his wife, who gains a good reputation in all circles. The peace of his house and his good management prepare him to be among the elders to judge well in the cases of others.

31.24.2.en: The wisdom of the virtuous woman is reflected in the life of her husband, for the building up of the house and adorning it with the righteousness of Christ makes her husband fit to be a dignified judge, who has his standing at the gates of the city where the courts are held.

31.25.0.en: She maketh fine linen, and selleth it; and delivereth girdles unto the Canaanite [24].

31.25.1.en: The virtuous woman does not make shirts for her family only, but also makes shirts which she sells for the benefit of the family. She also makes girdles which she offers for sale to those who come in distant caravans.

31.25.2.en: She points to the Church, which is clothed with the righteousness of Christ and bears witness to Him, and so offers to strangers the possibility of enjoying the same righteousness.

31.26.0.en: Strength and honour are her clothing; and she shall rejoice in time to come [25].

31.26.1.en: Since the virtuous woman enjoys spiritual righteousness, and her inner man is renewed day by day by the Holy Spirit of God, she does not fear the future, for she is in a faithful hand, and under the Spirit of God, who is able to overcome all difficulties.

31.26.2.en: She puts on our Lord Jesus, and hides in Him, and so she bears His splendor within her, which the world has no power to take from her.

31.27.0.en: She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue is the law of kindness [26].

31.27.1.en: Grace is poured out on the lips of the virtuous woman, so she always works on behalf of the Kingdom of God, as Priscilla did with her husband Aquila when they instructed Apollos in the Holy Spirit, of whom he had not heard before (Acts 18:26).

31.27.2.en: By the spirit of wisdom together with gentleness the virtuous woman builds up many souls.

31.27.3.en: * Mercy is found on the tongue of (Jesus), as He teaches the Law with mercy, as it is said of wisdom: "She bears on her tongue the law and mercy." Do not fear that you cannot fulfill the Law; flee to mercy.

31.27.4.en: * "She openeth her mouth with wisdom, and puts a rule (law) on her tongue," so she praises creation as creation, and the Creator as Creator, and the angels as angels, and the heavenly beings as heavenly, and the earthly as earthly, men as men, and animals as animals. There is no mixing, and nothing out of order, and she does not take the name of the Lord her God in vain, nor does she ascribe the nature of the creature to the Creator. She speaks of everything with an orderly method, so she does not set the lesser things above the more important, nor bring down the more important to the lesser.

31.28.s.en: G. Her care for her household

31.28.0.en: She looketh well to the ways of her household, and eateth not the bread of idleness [27].

31.28.1.en: Her serious care for her household obliges every member of the family to perform his role diligently in his relation with God and his relation with the rest of the family, especially the wife or mother. She works for them, and so she finds them vying in working for her.

31.28.2.en: She teaches that idleness leads to vice, therefore every member in the house has his work, that they may eat of the sweet bread of work, not the bread of sloth and idleness.

31.28.3.en: With the gentleness of her speech and the kindness of her conduct she remains watchful over the salvation of her household, working with all her strength for the building up of all, and she knows no slackness or idleness in this work.

31.28.4.en: * Our Lord Jesus Christ says: "The workman is worthy of his meat" - not everyone at all and however it may happen, but only the doer (Mt 10:10); and the Apostle Paul commands us to labor and work with our hands the thing which is good, that we may have to give to him that needeth (Eph 4:28). From this it is clear that we must work diligently, for it is not lawful for us to take worship as a pretext for idleness and for escaping office. Rather we must make it a subject of striving and many labors and patience in tribulations, that it may be granted to us also to say: "In weariness and painfulness, in watchings often, in hunger and thirst" (2 Cor 11:27). Such a course profits not only for the mortification of the body, but also for the practice of love of neighbor, that we may support needy brothers and provide them sustenance by our hands, according to what the Apostle taught in the Book of Acts, saying: "I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring ye ought to support the weak" (Acts 20:35). And again: "Rather let him labour, working with his hands the thing which is good, that he may have to give to him that needeth" (Eph 4:28). And so you will deserve to hear His words: "Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world: for I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink..." (Mt 25:34).

31.28.5.en: And I have no need to describe to you the gravity of the evil of idleness, when the Apostle commanded plainly: "If any would not work, neither should he eat" (2 Thess 3:10); for just as daily bread is necessary for every man, so toil according to his ability is necessary for him. Solomon did not write in vain in praise of the diligent woman: "She eateth not the bread of idleness" (Prov 31:27), and the Apostle also said of himself: "Neither did we eat any man's bread for nought; but wrought with labour and travail night and day, that we might not be chargeable to any of you" (2 Thess 3:8), although he had authority as a preacher of the Gospel to live of the Gospel (1 Cor 9:4, 14); indeed the Lord joins idleness with wickedness when He said: "Thou wicked and slothful servant" (Mt 25:26). Moreover, the wise Solomon not only praised the worker in what we have mentioned (Prov 31:27), but also rebuked the sluggard by comparing him with the lowest of the animals, saying: "Go to the ant, thou sluggard" (Prov 6:6). Therefore we must fear lest we too be rebuked in the day of judgment, because He who gave us the ability to work requires of us works suited to this ability. For He said: "To whom men have committed much, of him they will ask the more" (Lk 12:48).

31.28.6.en: And since some shrink from work on the pretext of prayers and the chanting of psalms, such people should know that there is a special time for everything, as the Preacher said: "To every thing there is a season" (Eccl 3:1).

31.28.7.en: * We must therefore work as far as possible, to share resources with those who lack them... There is no excuse for the lazy man who lives in idleness while he is able to work. Let him imitate those fish that cross the seas in a wonderful way in search of food.

31.29.s.en: H. Her honor and her outlook full of hope

31.29.0.en: Her children arise up, and call her blessed.

31.29.1.en: Her husband also, and he praiseth her [28].

31.29.2.en: This watchfulness over the salvation of the household may at times cause a kind of temporary distress, but soon all discover - young and old, the sons and the husband - that her presence in the house, her prayers, her vigils, her fasts for them and her prostrations (metanoias) are priceless treasures! So her children call her blessed, and her husband praises her.

31.29.3.en: Since she cares for the upbringing of her children, they see in their home a living icon of heaven, their souls rejoice, and they respect their mother and call her blessed. They carry within them the fear of the Lord and obedience to the divine commandment, with gentleness and kindness even in speaking with their mother.

31.29.4.en: * The religious wife is blessed. Let her praise the fear of the Lord; give her of the fruit of her lips, that her husband may be praised in the gates. Again: "A virtuous woman is a crown to her husband" (Prov 12:4). And also: [Many women built a house] (cf. Prov 14:1). You have learned what great commandments the prudent and loving wife receives from the Lord God.

31.30.0.en: Canons of the Apostles Many daughters have done virtuously, but thou excellest them all [29].

31.30.1.en: The Church of the New Testament surpassed, in her inner glory, the people of God of old, for it was said that the least in the Kingdom of Heaven is greater than St. John the Baptist (Mt 11:11). It was also said to the men of the New Testament that the Fathers and prophets desired to see what they see and to hear what they hear, and did not enjoy it as they do (Lk 10:24). The Church of the New Testament also surpassed the devout among the ancient Gentiles who walked according to the natural law.

31.30.2.en: St. John Chrysostom sees that the Church of the New Testament occupies the position of the devil before his fall, so she is counted as one of the greatest heavenly orders.

31.30.3.en: And St. Mary, the Mother of God, as the first and most perfect member of the Church, since the divine Word became incarnate of her by the Holy Spirit, surpassed those in heaven and those on earth.

31.30.4.en: Who is this who surpassed all the daughters who have done virtuously, but St. Mary, to whom the preceding characteristics apply, together with her enjoyment of the riches of the surpassing grace of God, since she bore the Word of God within her without the seed of man?!

31.30.5.en: * There is none like the Mother of God, for while dwelling on earth you became the mother of the Creator.

31.31.s.en: I. Her wisdom and inner beauty

31.31.0.en: Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised [30].

31.31.1.en: The true beauty of the virtuous wife does not lie in her outward features and delicacy, but in her fear of the Lord. For the fear of the Lord, when it reigns over the heart, reflects a divine beauty upon the soul that increases in splendor with time.

31.31.2.en: The beauty of the body is vain; sickness can spoil it and pains can shatter it, and by death it passes away completely. But the fear of the Lord is the refuge in which the soul takes shelter to live in a beauty that gives pleasure to God and the heavenly beings and also to men.

31.31.3.en: The virtuous wife is wise in all her conduct; every word that comes out of her mouth is weighed by the judgments of wisdom. She is prudent not only in her behavior but in her counsel to others. The law of love and kindness is engraved on her heart, declared in her words. Her heart is satisfied with what she enjoys of the earnest of the other life, and her hands work on behalf of heaven.

31.31.4.en: Outward beauty is deceitful, for it passes away with time, but the godliness of the virtuous woman increases in splendor with time, and reaches perfection in the great day of the Lord. It is said: "The king's daughter is all glorious within" (Ps 45).

31.31.5.en: The soul that receives the Lord Christ as her spiritual Bridegroom enjoys true beauty, for He pours His splendor upon her. Her all-beautiful Bridegroom says to her: "And thy renown went forth among the heathen for thy beauty: for it was perfect through my comeliness, which I had put upon thee, saith the Lord GOD" (Ezek 16:14). So the beauty of the bride is only a reflection of the beauty and splendor of the Bridegroom upon her.

31.31.6.en: * "Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; thou hast doves' eyes" (Song 1:15). You are fair and strong because you are made like him whom the song presents: "in thy glory and thy majesty" (Ps 45:4); you hear from your companion: "Forget also thine own people, and thy father's house; so shall the king greatly desire thy beauty" (Ps 45:10-11).

31.31.7.en: St. Jerome * It is fitting for the wife to follow her husband if she sees him standing beside God (Gen 18:11).

31.32.0.en: Origen Give her of the fruit of her hands; and let her own works praise her in the gates [31].

31.32.1.en: In the great day of the Lord the good works of the Church in the Lord will come forward to bear witness to her righteousness, and stand at the gates so that the heavenly beings may honor her for her faithfulness in her love for her heavenly Bridegroom and her patience in bearing witness to Him.

31.32.3.en: * You created my soul in Your image and likeness.

31.32.4.en: And You gave it dominion over the earthly creation.

31.32.5.en: You put all things under its feet.

31.32.6.en: In folly it clung to evil, and spoiled what it had received.

31.32.7.en: And in negligence it became drunk with the pleasures of the world.

31.32.8.en: Who can remove evil from me but You, O You who alone are good!

31.32.9.en: Who can turn me back from the drunkenness of this world, except the drunkenness of Your love?

31.32.10.en: * May I acquire You, O pearl of great price.

31.32.11.en: I hide You in my heart, the weak vessel.

31.32.12.en: And I enjoy Your manifestation within me, so that my soul becomes through You a heavenly queen, and Your Spirit prepares me as a bride adorned with heavenly things.

31.32.13.en: * Let me lean on Your breast, trusting in You, and You will strengthen me, and I will become through You a place of every confidence.

31.32.14.en: * You dwell within me by Your Holy Spirit, and I become a temple for You and a holy throne.

31.32.15.en: The enemy will not dare to creep in while You are within me.

31.32.16.en: Nor can sin draw me away while You are in my depths!

31.32.17.en: By You I am justified, and without You I am condemned!

31.32.18.en: * Let Your hands strengthen me, that I may work.

31.32.19.en: Laziness will not creep in upon me, for I find delight in working by You and with You and for You.

31.32.20.en: And You, the Creator of all, work for my sake; how then shall I not work for Your Kingdom?

31.32.21.en: * Grant me fellowship in Your attributes, that my heart may be filled with love and tenderness.

31.32.22.en: Let my soul groan with the groans of every heart.

31.32.23.en: And let my depths cry out with the cries of every sufferer.

31.32.24.en: Let me see the whole world as my beloved home.

31.32.25.en: I long to serve all, and let my hands be spread out in prayer for all.

31.32.27.en: Your indwelling pours into the soul a beauty that does not fade!

31.32.28.en: Your manifestation shines with light within me!
